facts.statement: Cantioscyllium is known mainly from isolated teeth, though the genus was named based on a partial skeleton found in Late Cretaceous England.
facts.quote: It is known mainly from isolated teeth, but was named on a partial skeleton from the Late Cretaceous of England.

facts.statement: Cantioscyllium fossils are found throughout the Late Cretaceous of the eastern United States, including the Severn Formation in Maryland, the Tar Heel and Peedee formations in North Carolina, and the Campanian of New Jersey.
facts.quote: They are uncommon but present throughout the late cretaceous of the eastern United States, including the Severn Formation of Maryland, the Tar Heel and Peedee formations of North Carolina, and Campanian of New Jersey.

facts.statement: Fossils of Cantioscyllium have also been found in the Western Interior Seaway and western Europe.
facts.quote: It is also known from the Western Interior Seaway and western Europe.

facts.statement: The species C. hashimiaensis is known from the Santonian period of Jordan.
facts.quote: C. hashimiaensis is known from the Santonian of Jordan.

facts.statement: The species C. alhaulfi dates to the Barremian period.
facts.quote: C. alhaulfi is from the Barremian.

facts.statement: Cantioscyllium belongs to the family Ginglymostomatidae.
Cantioscyllium is classified within the class Chondrichthyes.
Cantioscyllium lived from the Kimmeridgian to the Maastrichtian, spanning from 152.21 to 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Kimmeridgian to Maastrichtian (152.21 to 66 million years ago)

rejected.statement: Cantioscyllium is an extinct genus of nurse shark that lived during the Mesozoic era.
